title: Set 289

sentences.ko: 월세가 한 달에 200달러씩 오른다고 해서 좀 더 외곽 쪽 집들을 알아보고 있어. 아니 돈은 아끼겠지만 다들 있는 데서 한 40분 거리가 될 거고, 그러다 아예 밖에 안 나가게 될까 봐 좀 걱정돼.
sentences.text: My rent's going up two hundred a month, so I've been looking at places a little farther out. I mean, I'd save money, but I'd be like forty minutes from everybody, and I'm kind of worried I'd just stop going out.

alts.text: Rent's going up two hundred a month, so I've been checking out places a bit farther out. Like, I'd save money, but I'd be forty minutes from everybody, and I'm kinda scared I'd just never go out anymore.

My rent is increasing by two hundred dollars a month, so I have been looking at places a little farther from the city. I would save money, but I would be about forty minutes away from everyone, and I am somewhat concerned that I would simply stop going out.

sentences.note: **a little farther out** 는 도심에서 좀 더 떨어진 외곽 쪽을 말할 때 씁니다. **I mean** 은 말을 고쳐 잇거나 덧붙일 때 쓰는 말버릇으로, 아니 또는 그러니까 정도의 느낌입니다.

sentences.ko: 아니야 엄마, 밥 잘 먹고 있다니까, 진짜야. 거의 매일 저녁 해 먹고 있어. 그래, 매일은 아닐 수도 있는데, 그래도 목요일쯤부터 피자는 안 먹었으니까 그것도 어디야.
sentences.text: No, Mom, I'm eating fine, I promise. I've been cooking almost every night. Okay, maybe not every night, but I haven't had pizza since like Thursday, so that counts for something.

alts.text: Mom, seriously, I'm eating fine. I cook pretty much every night. Okay, not every night, but I haven't had pizza since Thursday, so that's gotta count for something, right?
Mother, I assure you that I am eating well. I have been cooking nearly every evening. Admittedly, not every evening, but I have not had pizza since Thursday, so I believe that counts for something.

sentences.note: **that counts for something** 은 대단하진 않아도 그래도 의미가 있다, 그것도 어디냐는 뜻입니다. **since like Thursday** 의 like 는 대략, 한 정도라는 뜻으로 붙이는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: 부모님 안부 전화에서 잘 지낸다고 둘러대기

sentences.ko: 거기 원래 내 최애 가게였는데, 작년에 주인이 바뀌고 나서는 음식이 다 냉동 같은 맛이 나. 그날만 별로였길 바라면서 지난주에 다시 가 봤는데, 아니더라, 똑같았어. 그래서 이제 거기는 안 가려고.
sentences.text: That place used to be my favorite, but they got new owners last year and now everything tastes kind of frozen. I went back last week hoping it was just a bad night, but nope, it was the same, so I think I'm done with it.

alts.text: I used to love that place, but new owners took over last year and now it all tastes kinda frozen. Went back last week thinking maybe it was just a bad night, but nope, same thing. I'm done with it.

That restaurant was once my favorite, but it came under new ownership last year, and now everything tastes as though it was frozen. I returned last week in the hope that it had simply been a bad evening, but it was the same, so I do not intend to go back.

sentences.note: **I'm done with it** 은 이제 그만두겠다, 더는 안 하겠다는 뜻입니다. **a bad night** 는 가게나 주방이 그날따라 유독 잘 못한 날이라는 뜻이고, **nope** 은 no 를 가볍게 말하는 표현입니다.

sentences.ko: 드디어 손목 검사를 받았는데, 의사가 별거 아니래. 타자만 좀 덜 치면 된대. 근데 그게 사실상 내 일 전부거든, 그래서 타자 덜 치는 건 아무래도 못 할 것 같아.
sentences.text: So I finally got my wrist checked, and the doctor said it's nothing serious, I just need to stop typing so much. Which, you know, is basically my whole job, so I don't really see that happening.

alts.text: Finally had the doctor look at my wrist, and it's nothing serious, I just gotta stop typing so much. Which, I mean, is pretty much my whole job, so yeah, that's not gonna happen.
I finally had my wrist examined, and the doctor said it is nothing serious; I simply need to type less. However, that is essentially my entire job, so I do not expect that to happen.

sentences.note: **got my wrist checked** 는 손목을 검사받았다는 뜻으로, get + 대상 + checked 형태로 진료나 점검을 받을 때 씁니다. **I don't really see that happening** 은 그렇게 될 것 같지 않다는 뜻입니다.
sentences.situation: 병원 갔다 온 얘기 가볍게 하기

sentences.ko: 일요일에 한 1년 만에 처음으로 달리기를 했는데, 뛰는 내내 기분이 너무 좋았어. 근데 월요일에 일어났더니 온몸이 다 아프더라. 내 몸은 나만큼 신나지 않았나 봐.
sentences.text: I went for a run on Sunday for the first time in like a year, and I felt amazing the whole time. But then I woke up Monday and everything hurt, so I guess my body wasn't as excited about it as I was.

alts.text: Went for a run Sunday, first time in like a year, and I felt awesome the whole way. Then Monday I woke up and everything hurt, so I guess my body wasn't as into it as I was.

I went running on Sunday for the first time in about a year, and I felt wonderful the entire time. However, when I woke up on Monday, everything ached, so I suppose my body was not as enthusiastic about it as I was.

sentences.note: **for the first time in like a year** 는 한 1년 만에 처음으로라는 뜻입니다. **wasn't as excited about it as I was** 는 나만큼 신이 나지 않았다는 뜻으로, 몸을 사람처럼 말하는 농담입니다.

reviewed: 1번 한국어: '오른대서' 는 남에게 전해 들은 말처럼 읽혀서 '오른다고 해서' 로 고침
3번 note: a bad night 를 '운이 나빴던 날' 로 설명했는데, 여기서는 가게(주방)가 그날따라 잘 못한 날이라는 뜻이라 맞게 고침
4번 한국어: '그럴 일은 별로 없을 것 같아' 는 영어의 I don't really see that happening(그렇게는 못 할 것 같다)과 결이 달라서 '타자를 덜 치는 건 못 할 것 같아' 로 고침
